ketovore.text: Ketovore is followed by people who want keto-style fat loss with the simplicity of a meat-centred plate, aiming for a leaner body and less bloat. The hybrid label has no trials of its own; evidence comes from keto and low-carb diet research generally.

eat-like-a-bodybuilder-rice-chicken-broc.text: Users adopt the rice, chicken and broccoli template to gain muscle or cut fat with very few food decisions, building a leaner, more muscular physique. The underlying principles of protein intake and calorie control are well studied; the specific three-food menu is a convention rather than a tested protocol.

chain: Steady fat loss or muscle gain
meal-prep.text: Meal prep is used to hit calorie and protein targets consistently, which supports fat loss or muscle gain and a better physique over time. Small studies link it to better eating habits; its direct effect on appearance has not been measured.

hot-sauce-thermogenics-spicy-food.text: Forum posters eat chili and hot sauce, or take capsaicin supplements, hoping to speed metabolism and trim body fat for a leaner look. Capsaicin has been studied for appetite and energy expenditure, with small effects reported and weak evidence for visible weight loss.

sea-moss-chlorella-spirulina.text: Sea moss gels and chlorella or spirulina powders are promoted as superfoods for glowing skin and energy. The nutrient content of the algae is documented, while appearance effects have not been tested in trials and rest largely on marketing and anecdote.

chain: Claimed better nutrition and gut health
greens-powders-ag1.text: Greens powders such as AG1 are taken as a daily all-in-one supplement, with users crediting them for better skin, digestion and energy. Brand-supported trials are small and focus on nutrient status; appearance effects have not been tested.

tapeworm-sanitized-parasite-diet.text: The tapeworm diet is a fringe weight-loss idea in which people look to a parasite to reduce how many calories they absorb, aiming for a thinner body. It is untested as a weight-loss method and is not an accepted medical approach.

chewing-and-spitting.text: Chewing and spitting appears in appearance communities as a way to enjoy food while avoiding its calories for a leaner look. In clinical literature it is documented as a behaviour seen in eating disorders and a marker of severity, not as a studied appearance method.

chain: Weight loss and a leaner look
extended-fasting-dopamine-fasts.text: Extended fasts are used for rapid weight loss, while dopamine fasts, which cut phone use, gaming and porn, are promoted for focus, discipline and a mental reset that supports habits like training and sleep. Food fasting is studied for weight loss; the behavioural version is loosely defined and untested for looks.

alkaline-water-alkaline-diet.text: Followers of the alkaline diet and alkaline water say they improve skin, energy and general health by shifting body pH. The diet's emphasis on fruit and vegetables is conventional, while the pH mechanism and any appearance benefit have not been shown in studies.

detox-teas-juice-cleanses.text: Users take detox teas and juice cleanses for clearer skin, a leaner face and reduced bloating. Short-term scale and bloat changes are commonly reported; the claim of removing toxins is not supported by reviews, and skin effects are untested.

fruit-juice-cleanse.text: Juice cleanses are done over a few days as a reset, with people hoping for glowing skin, less bloat and quick weight loss. Short-term weight change is expected from reduced calories, while the detox and skin claims have no published research behind them.

chain: Swap seed oils for olive oil
Different fatty acid and polyphenol intake
cold-pressed-oils-olive-oil.text: Looksmaxxers promote extra virgin olive oil and other cold-pressed oils as a replacement for refined seed oils, citing skin and general health. Olive oil has regulator-qualified heart-health claims; its effect on appearance has not been tested.

chain: Dairy fats instead of seed oils
butter-ghee.text: Butter and ghee are promoted in ancestral and looksmaxxing diet circles as alternatives to vegetable oils, linked to skin health and hormone support. Appearance effects have not been studied; guidelines address them mainly through saturated fat.

grass-fed-beef-ethical-sourcing.text: Grass-fed beef is favoured for protein, omega-3 and CLA content and for ethical sourcing, as part of eating for muscle and skin. Fatty acid differences from grain-fed beef are measured; appearance benefits specific to grass-fed beef are unstudied.

sardines-oily-fish.text: Sardines and other oily fish are eaten as a cheap source of omega-3 fats, B12 and protein, with users linking them to better skin. Omega-3 intake is widely studied for health; skin benefits from eating oily fish were not tested in the sources reviewed.

eggs-egg-yolk.text: Eggs and yolks are a staple of bodybuilding and appearance diets as a cheap, complete protein with fat and choline, supporting muscle gain. Egg protein quality is well documented; the appearance effect comes through overall protein and calorie intake.

oats-rice-and-chicken-carbs-for-bulking.text: Lifters build a bulk around oats, rice and chicken to eat in a calorie surplus affordably and add muscle for a bigger physique. The link between positive energy balance and muscle growth is well established; the specific foods are a convention.

chain: Better training and recovery, more muscle
sweet-potato-carb-timing.text: Lifters schedule carbs such as sweet potato around training to fuel sessions and speed recovery, in pursuit of more muscle. Glycogen replacement after exercise is studied, while the benefit of exact timing for physique is debated.

eating-disorder-adjacent-restriction-thi.text: Some appearance communities discuss extreme restriction to reach a gaunt or very lean look, often through thinspo content. Medical groups treat this pattern as eating disorder risk, and it is described in clinical literature rather than studied as an appearance method.

pre-workout-stim-stacks.text: Lifters take caffeine-based pre-workout blends to push training harder and more often, aiming for more muscle and a leaner physique. Caffeine has the strongest evidence for performance; the other ingredients show mixed results and no appearance trials exist.

body-dysmorphic-disorder-bdd.text: BDD is discussed in looksmaxxing communities as the clinical condition behind obsessive focus on appearance flaws, including a muscle dysmorphia subtype. It is a recognised psychiatric disorder with established treatments in CBT and SSRIs.

cbt-for-bdd.text: CBT for BDD is the talk therapy people with appearance preoccupation are directed to, using exposure and response prevention to reduce checking and distress. It is the best-studied psychological treatment for BDD, with trials on symptom reduction rather than on looks.

ssris-for-bdd.text: SSRIs are antidepressants prescribed for BDD to ease obsessive preoccupation with a perceived flaw, and are mentioned in looksmaxxing forums in that context. They are studied for BDD symptoms; they are a medical treatment and not an appearance tool.

mirror-checking-mirror-avoidance.text: Forum users describe mirror checking and avoidance as habits that feed fixation on perceived flaws. Both are documented as behaviours in BDD, with CBT targeting them directly.

reassurance-seeking-rate-me-threads.text: Rate-me threads are used to get outside opinions on facial attractiveness and what to improve. Clinically, repeated reassurance seeking is listed among BDD behaviours, alongside mirror checking and comparing.

blackpill.text: The blackpill is an incel-born framework holding that looks and genetics largely set dating and social outcomes, and looksmaxxers debate whether it motivates or discourages self-improvement. Research shows attractiveness affects outcomes, while its fatalistic conclusions are a belief.

chain: Different views on what to improve
redpill-bluepill-purplepill-frameworks.text: The pill metaphors are used in online communities to label worldviews on dating and status, with the blackpill being the looks-deterministic one that looksmaxxing often engages. They are cultural frameworks rather than studied models.

chain: Different treatment in hiring and dating
lookism.text: Lookism is the term for judging people by appearance, and it is core vocabulary in looksmaxxing as the reason many men work on their looks. Sociology and economics research reports real but variable attractiveness effects in hiring, dating and elsewhere.

chain: Structural change to face or body
hardmaxxing.text: Hardmaxxing is looksmaxxing slang for invasive methods such as surgery, fillers and off-label drugs, used for changes like jaw, nose or skin that softer methods do not reach. Established procedures produce visible results, while DIY and fringe variants are poorly studied.
